title: QUIC RFC 9000 0-RTT Packet Format Focused Proof
purpose: Describe the focused proof boundary for RFC 9000 0-RTT long-header packet-format requirements.
design_summary: The 0-RTT packet-format proof is decomposed into requirement-home tests that exercise the existing long-header parser and 0-RTT packet builder directly. The parser validates version 1 long-header shape, connection-ID length limits, varint Length fields, and packet-number length consistency. The builder proof covers client first-flight 0-RTT emission, packet-number progression, 0-RTT suppression after 1-RTT processing, ACK exclusion, and remembered-limit error classification.
data_and_state_considerations: The slice does not introduce new packet-format runtime behavior. It makes the existing parser and builder responsibilities explicit through focused positive, negative, and edge proofs so generated triage no longer depends on broad header fuzz/property tests for S17P2P3 closure.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Shortest structurally valid 0-RTT packets are accepted when the Length field covers the encoded packet number.
Length fields shorter than the encoded packet number are rejected.
Destination and source connection IDs are proven at zero-byte, twenty-byte, and over-limit boundaries.
0-RTT first-flight emission remains after the Initial packet and is suppressed when early-data readiness is absent or 1-RTT processing has begun.
ACK payloads remain outside the repository-owned bootstrap 0-RTT emission path.
alternatives_considered: Keep broad header parser fuzz/property tests as the only evidence; rejected because the current triage rules require narrow requirement-home proof.
Add new parser behavior for 0-RTT-only wrappers; rejected because the existing long-header parser already owns the wire-format checks needed for this slice.
Claim full remembered-limit enforcement for all early-data surfaces; rejected because this slice proves the existing stream remembered-limit floor only.
risks: 0-RTT packet decryption/opening is still outside this structural parser proof.
The slice does not claim interop readiness for arbitrary early-data application payloads.
The remembered-limit proof remains stream-state scoped rather than a complete server early-data policy matrix.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design covers focused 0-RTT packet-format and current repository-owned emission proof for S17P2P3. It does not broaden TLS 0-RTT acceptance policy, transport-parameter remembered-limit policy, or packet-protection cryptographic validation.
